rv.q: It sometimes feels a little rushed, but it is a powerful and humane piece that establishes Rwothomack and Zidan as compelling performers. Due to play in New York after its UK tour, this is a story with real international resonance, and demonstrates how the Bank initiative is already bearing creative fruit.
The team do a great job at finding a balance between highlighting injustice in the world whilst also bringing out moments for light humour in what could otherwise be a very emotionally heavy show.
It’s powerfully played by two great performers but in the end LINES is a show that you should see to get you educated to understand postcolonial lives.

cn.t: Critics praise "Lines" for its powerful dramatic insight into prison systems across Uganda and Palestine, with John Rwothomack and Fidaa Zidan delivering compelling explorations of their nations' complex histories through movement and text.
